reviews.title: Designed to be deleted, yet here I am.
reviews.text:
You know, I’ve been on this app for a few years now, and I have yet to actually delete it… which, ironically, is the entire selling point of the platform.

As a gay man, I find myself questioning why some of my supposedly most compatible matches are straight-identifying men.

I won’t blame Hinge itself for the quality of men on the platform. That’s an entirely separate conversation. However, I do believe there should be a greater emphasis on accountability and the actual experiences users have with one another.

I’d love to see a more comprehensive feedback system that goes beyond the pre-existing options, particularly when two individuals unmatch. Something that specifically asks about the quality of communication, consistency, respect, and overall experience. Ideally, recurring patterns of negative interactions could influence how prominently certain profiles are recommended, provided there are safeguards against dishonest or retaliatory feedback.

And I say all of this as a knowingly flawed individual myself. I’m certainly not exempt from criticism, nor do I expect perfection from anyone else.

But for an app that markets itself as the more intentional approach to dating, I find it disappointing that, several years later, I’m still here questioning whether that intention is genuinely reflected in the experience.

I’m not satisfied, much less impressed.

reviews.title: Unfair perma ban based on unsubstantiated  allegations
reviews.text:
I was permanently banned from Hinge following an absolute disaster of a date with someone who made what I maintain was a completely false allegation against me.

During the date, I discovered that this individual was scheduled to appear in court the following month in connection with a fraud matter. Needless to say, the date went downhill from there.

I appealed the ban and submitted substantial supporting evidence, including screenshots of text conversations, video footage, and publicly available court records relating to the individual involved.

Despite providing this information, Hinge showed no apparent interest in reviewing the circumstances fairly. The response was essentially, “Tough luck. Permanent ban.”

What frustrates me most isn’t simply being banned. It’s the complete lack of transparency, accountability, or meaningful opportunity to defend myself against an allegation I dispute.

Apparently, an accusation is enough to permanently remove someone from the platform, regardless of the evidence they provide in response.

If you’re considering Hinge, understand that your account can be permanently removed with little explanation and seemingly no meaningful recourse.

reviews.title: Waste of time
reviews.text:
Hinge markets itself as the app “designed to be deleted,” but it’s designed to keep you swiping and paying. The free tier is crippled to push you toward the subscription, and even then the results don’t match the price.
You get a handful of likes a day, so you spend more time curating than connecting. The “Most Compatible” feature feels random, and the algorithm keeps surfacing the same profiles while the people you’d actually click with never appear. Likes from people you can’t see are locked behind the paywall, which feels like a pay-to-reveal gimmick.
Conversations die quickly. Matches go silent after one message, and profiles that look active are often abandoned. Ghosting is rampant and there’s no real accountability. Reporting fake or inactive accounts seems to go nowhere, and support replies are slow and generic.
Verification is inconsistent, so you still run into photos that don’t resemble the person. For a platform that charges premium prices, the experience is inconsistent and the value just isn’t there.
If you want meaningful connections, you’ll likely get better odds putting your money into real-world events and activities. Two stars would be generous, but one is the honest rating.

Shame on you Match group leadership. You have so much bad karma coming your way due to how hard you’ve made it for ppl to find a partner, marry and have kids. It’s too hard, so ppl are living lives of loneliness. That’s your karma. Shame, shame, shame.

This, however, started a ban loop across the Match.com network, where my Tinder account would be flagged and banned, which would then cause my Hinge account to be flagged and banned due to a flag on the Tinder side, and so on. 

This was 18 months ago. The Tinder side is completely fixed, and has been working fine for 10 months, as they figured out the initial ban was made in error. Hinge however - I follow up every few months but either receive no reply to my tickets or a generic automated response. 

It’s a shame as it’s probably the best dating app available, but the support side is severely lacking when something goes wrong. The Hinge brand is built around support, safety and respect in the dating community, but my experience has been quite the opposite of that - it’s quite distressing to have done nothing wrong yet be excluded from their app with zero support.

reviews.title: Payer un abonnement et repayer pour être visible …😈
reviews.text:
Déçue par le fonctionnement de Hinge malgré un abonnement payant.

J’ai souscrit un abonnement et j’utilise réellement l’application : profil complet, Likes envoyés régulièrement à des profils correspondant à mes critères… et pourtant, quasiment aucun retour ni match.

Je suis parfaitement consciente que payer un abonnement ne garantit évidemment pas de plaire ni d’obtenir des matchs. Ce n’est pas le problème. Ce qui me dérange, c’est le manque total de transparence sur la visibilité réelle des Likes envoyés.

Hinge propose parallèlement des options payantes supplémentaires, comme les Roses ou les Priority Likes, permettant justement d’être davantage mis en avant. Cela pose forcément la question : quelle visibilité obtient-on réellement avec l’abonnement que l’on paie déjà ?

J’ai contacté le support précisément à ce sujet afin qu’il vérifie mon compte et m’explique si mes Likes sont normalement distribués et visibles. À ce jour, je n’ai obtenu aucune réponse précise sur ce point.

Je trouve donc l’expérience particulièrement frustrante : payer un abonnement sans pouvoir savoir si les Likes envoyés bénéficient réellement d’une visibilité correcte, puis devoir encore payer davantage pour être prioritaire, donne franchement l’impression d’un système avant tout conçu pour multiplier les options payantes.

reviews.title: Banned - no cause
reviews.text:
I was banned with no explanation. 

Likely you’re thinking: “toxic guy was toxic and now just wants to complain”. 

I can’t prove otherwise - I’m just a guy writing a one star review.

I’ll simply say that it’s not the case: I’m a regular, sincere dater who was trying to meet someone special and turned to apps like any other mid 30s hopeful. I suspect I got flagged by the algorithm for some payment issue or it was a fraudulent report. 

Regardless of the reason for my ban, Hinge has been a dating app on the decline from its golden era. Fake profiles, one-word profiles, tinder-esque engagements, weaponised reporting, insta-bans and an opaque appeals process are frictions that normal people will quickly move on from.  

I have no doubt Hinge will continue on as a giant in the dating space for a while yet -
These things have an inertia unto themselves. Though I suspect it will increasingly replace regular, engaged and motivated daters with bots, fake profiles and actual toxic people (who will obviously work to evade any ban and don’t mind friction). Match Group will continue to inflate new user data for shareholders and harvest invaluable personal data in the meantime. The question is which app will capture sincere daters next?

I’ll take my cash there and see you there too (or in the real world)😌.

reviews.title: Support that never actually helps
reviews.text:
Hinge used to be a great app, but my recent experience has been extremely disappointing. My profile suddenly went from getting normal engagement to almost none, so I contacted support multiple times asking them to investigate whether there was an issue with my account’s visibility.

Instead of receiving a meaningful investigation, I was repeatedly sent the same generic copy-and-paste response saying “everything is working as expected.” None of my specific questions were answered, and it felt like no one had actually read my messages.

Eventually, I deleted my account out of frustration. When I reached out afterward, I was simply told that deleted accounts cannot be restored. At no point did anyone acknowledge or properly investigate the concerns that led me to delete it in the first place.

I understand that not everyone gets matches, and I’m not asking for guaranteed results. My issue is with the quality of customer support. If users report a potential account issue, they deserve an actual investigation—not automated template replies.

Until Hinge improves how it handles customer support and user concerns, I can’t recommend this app.

reviews.title: Definitely designed to be deleted!
reviews.text: When I used hinge it seemed like it was very rare to find anyone with similar interests or values as me. Turns out it’s  intentionally designed that way just to keep you using the app, because uncertainty accelerates addiction. It would be very easy to implement an algorithm that shows people with similar prompts to you in your feed, but that’s not good for business. At the end of the day you are a customer. Your loneliness or want for approval is an opportunity for profit. They don’t care about your happiness, they care about your wallets. To whoever is reading this, I care… I deleted this app months ago and worked on myself instead, and it was the best decision. I met someone at uni who I have so much in common with, more than any of the potential matches from hinge. All you need is a bit of patience and hope. Keep your eyes and heart open to the people around you, instead of focused on your phone. Intimacy is about growing more than you could by yourself. So in the meantime, grow as much as you can on your own until you meet that person. Peace and groundedness come not from externals, but from within. <3

reviews.title: Betrug
reviews.text:
Habe die App nach einem halben Jahr auf meinem neuen Handy installiert und meine Bilder „geupdated“ und mir eine Woche das Plusabo geholt. Habe am ersten Tag ein paar Likes verteilt und einer Person eine Songempfehlung auf ihrem Profil hinterlassen, da sie danach fragte. Am nächsten Tag wurde ich permanent gesperrt ohne eine Erklärung. Zum Mitschreiben per Gesetz ist es in der EU verboten Konten zu sperren ohne eine konkrete Erklärung zu geben (DSA). Nachdem ich mehrfach per Email verwundert darauf hingewiesen habe und im Detail erklärt habe, was ich genau in der Zeit vor der Sperrung getan habe und wie es dort keinen Verstoß habe geben können, kamen jeweils nur 2 automatisierte Antworten mit keiner Auskunft und das ich nach der letzten Email bewusst ignoriert werden würde in Zukunft. Ich habe nichtmal einen Like geschweige denn ein Match gehabt und konnte nur Likes verteilen und einen Song bei einer extra gestellten Frage einer Person empfehlen und das scheint in dieser App dann eine Kontosperrung zur Folge zu haben. Komplett willkürlich, komplett intransparent, komplett illegal in der EU. Habe die Bundesnetzagentur auf die Firma aufmerksam gemacht, aber das Ergebnis wird Monate dauern. 

Unseriöser kann man nicht handeln, hoffe die Bundesnetzagentur wird eine saftige Geldstrafe verhängen für gebrochenes Recht.

reviews.title: Tu te réveil et tu es ban
reviews.text:
Hinge a un gros problème de transparence concernant les bannissements. De nombreux utilisateurs se retrouvent exclus définitivement de l’application sans explication précise, sans preuve fournie et sans savoir quelle règle aurait été enfreinte. Le système semble parfois reposer sur des signalements ou des décisions automatisées qui peuvent entraîner des erreurs, sans véritable possibilité pour l’utilisateur de comprendre ou de se défendre quand il a rien fait. 

Bannir un compte est une décision lourde puisque c’est définitif, surtout sur une application de rencontre où des conversations, des connexions et parfois des opportunités réelles disparaissent du jour au lendemain. Une modération efficace est nécessaire, mais elle doit aussi être juste : les utilisateurs méritent au minimum une explication claire, un vrai examen du dossier et un processus d’appel transparent.  

Actuellement, l’impression laissée est celle d’un système opaque où un utilisateur peut être sanctionné sans savoir pourquoi ni comment corriger un éventuel problème. Hinge devrait améliorer sa communication et surtout son système de bannissement défaillant afin d’offrir davantage de garanties contre les erreurs de modération.

As a “fully paid member” it is extremely frustrating to not know what has happened with a “like”.

You spend time and effort in writing a thoughtful message to a lady but never know if:

1. They have seen it and declined
2. It’s been seen and left sitting
3. Never seen it and it becomes archived 

As a PAID up member, I think it’s reasonable to at least know if your message has been read (plain common courtesy) and declined rather than it “unseen and timing out”. 

You should also indicate paid from non paid members so users can determine if it is worth spending time and effort in writing and sending someone a thoughtful message!! 

Also, why are you limiting the potential matches. 
There could be matches for today opposites and you are stopping those from happening. 

Unlikely to renew at this stage  unless this is addressed. I would recommend to all users to not renew and waste time on here if “common courtesy” isn’t applied

reviews.title: Extremely disappointed with Hinge’s moderation and appeals process.
reviews.text:
My account was permanently banned without any meaningful explanation, despite never knowingly violating the platform’s guidelines. The only unusual interaction I can recall was ending communication with a match who started asking me for money. Instead of protecting users from suspicious behavior, it seems the reporting system can be abused without proper investigation.

What’s most concerning is the complete lack of transparency. A company that asks users to invest time, effort, and often money into its platform should at least provide a clear reason when taking such a serious action. Instead, users are left with generic responses and no real opportunity to defend themselves.

If Hinge is confident in its decisions, it should have no problem conducting a genuine manual review and explaining the basis for a ban. Until then, it’s difficult to trust that innocent users won’t be removed based on false or malicious reports.

I want to start by stating something fundamental: this is a dating app. Basic personal questions and discussions around comfort, boundaries, and physical intimacy are a normal and necessary part of dating. Asking and confirming these things respectfully before proceeding is not misconduct — it is called consent.
Despite this, my account was permanently banned without any warning or explanation, even though I carefully followed every guideline published on the website. I did not engage in sexual, explicit, transactional, or inappropriate conversations. Any personal or physical topics were discussed respectfully and only after clear mutual consent.
What is infuriating is that following the written rules appears meaningless if a single report is filed. Is a user banned simply because someone reports them, without a proper review of the actual conversation and its context? If all stated guidelines were followed, on what basis is a permanent ban justified?
This points to a deeply flawed moderation process — one where reports seem to outweigh facts, context, or evidence. Paying users are removed without clarity, accountability, or even an opportunity to correct anything. That is not fair moderation; that is arbitrary enforcement.

I’m giving this app 1 star because of how unempathetic and inhuman the experience has been. After building real connections and talking to people sincerely, my entire account was suddenly removed — along with every match and message — without a clear reason or any meaningful explanation.

These weren’t bots or random profiles. These were real people, real conversations, real moments that I invested time and emotion into. It’s shocking how easily they can erase everything you’ve built on the app, as if your interactions don’t matter at all.

During my short time on the platform, I had set very clear age and preference parameters; however, those preferences were not acknowledged at all. I kept receiving matches far outside my selected age range, most of them much older or much  younger than me, which made the experience feel suspicious and inconsistent with what I had chosen. As a data analyst my self something felt off about the app. And despite this, I was inundated with over 160 messages in my first week, which made the sudden account removal even more confusing. 

Rather than investigating at my request or clarifying the issue, Hinge provided  no meaningful explanation, and I feel my account was wrongfully targeted and removed without cause. This experience has made me lose trust in the platform’s integrity, transparency, fairness, and ability to follow its own guidelines.
